comparison: Perfect claim overlap (C10, C113-C114) regarding the improved sgRNA scoring system. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of validation data ('will be systematically tested in future studies'), while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting the improvement as part of overall methodological advances without raising concerns about validation.

Perfect claim overlap (C23, C115-C118) on the hybrid gene replacement approach. Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes it's a proof-of-concept rather than extensive validation, while peer reviewers affirm the demonstration across three Leishmania species without concerns.

Perfect claim overlap (C24-C25, C129) on forward-looking impact statements. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval acknowledges these are speculative but reasonable given demonstrated improvements, while peer reviewers strongly endorse the potential for large-scale screens and utility to the research community.

High claim overlap (87.5% Jaccard) on T7 RNAP promoter optimization (C9, C48-C53). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative improvements (7 vs 33 days, no growth defects), while peer reviewers highlight reduced toxicity and retained editing efficiency as part of the meticulously-developed strategy.

Strong claim overlap (57.7% Jaccard) on pooled screen results (C13-C22, C97-C112). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed technical validation (24 targeting sgRNAs, 15 controls, ~25,000 cells/sgRNA), while peer reviewers confirm the small-scale loss-of-function screen successfully identified expected growth phenotypes.

Moderate claim overlap (50% Jaccard) on Cas12a integration system (C59-C69). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details the ~25-fold improvement and independence from homology flank length, while peer reviewers emphasize the 400-fold transfection efficiency improvement and compelling documentation of AsCas12a usefulness.

Partial claim overlap (27.3% Jaccard) on combined CBE-Cas12a system (C11, C72-C76). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on the 400-fold transfection efficiency improvement (1/70 cells) and complete tdTomato depletion, while peer reviewers confirm the efficiency improvement and integration usefulness across multiple figures.

Minimal claim overlap (C12 only) on the key transfection efficiency metric. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval treats this as a standalone quantitative achievement (400-fold improvement to 1/70 cells), while peer reviewers incorporate it into broader validation of the Cas12a integration approach.

Partial claim overlap (35.3% Jaccard) on PF16 targeting experiments (C81-C84, C86-C87). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details rapid editing (6 days) and notes the L. mexicana reversal with growth defect, while peer reviewers affirm efficient editing across three Leishmania species without raising concerns.

Partial claim overlap (37.5% Jaccard) on integration patterns (C94-C96). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes species differences in integration (single-copy in L. mexicana vs. multiple guides in some L. donovani/L. major clones), while peer reviewers accept this as ensuring single sgRNA cassette integration with high efficiency.

Partial claim overlap (29.4% Jaccard) on integration characterization (C88-C92). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed sequencing validation (ONT/Illumina, read coverage analysis), while peer reviewers accept the overall editing capacity across species as part of the meticulously-developed strategy.

Minor claim overlap (14.3% Jaccard) on combined system results (C70-C71, C78). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on tdTomato depletion and library representation calculations, while peer reviewers emphasize the overall editing efficiency across three Leishmania species.

OpenEval evaluates background/motivation claims (C1-C3, C26-C36, C119-C126) as SUPPORTED, establishing biological and technical challenges with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these introductory context claims.

OpenEval evaluates prior CBE system description and limitations (C4-C8, C37-C47) as SUPPORTED, all citing Engstler and Beneke 2023. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these baseline comparison claims.

OpenEval evaluates trade-offs of dual-construct system (C127-C128) as SUPPORTED, noting both disadvantages (requiring stable cell line) and advantages (efficient integration). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this balanced assessment.
